newsitem.title: BRAZIL: CVRD shrugs off report on gold, copper finds.
newsitem.headline: CVRD shrugs off report on gold, copper finds.

text.p: Brazilian state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) said it could not comment on newspaper claims that a geological report on its mining operations in northern Brazil confirmed huge new gold and copper finds.

CVRD Market relations officer Marcos Antonio Pinto said the company was unable to confirm or deny the contents of the geological assessment of the Carajas mining area cited in O Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper because the report was not relayed to CVRD.
O Estado de Sao Paulo said the report by Canadian geologist Robert Mason revealed that the Carajas region in Para state contains an unusual number of world class deposits.
Pinto said the report was compiled in October last year for the consortium which is evaluating CVRD's mining operations ahead of the companies privatization later this year.
Pinto said it was nothing new that the company had found a new gold deposit at Igarape-Bahia in the Carajas region, which was announced in October.

"There is a gold deposit which is promising but it is too early to say at this point how large it is," he said. "We have only carried out one third of the survey work necessary to establish the size of the deposit."
Pinto said it would be another three months before CVRD could say with relative certainty how large the deposit really is. ((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
